This result indicated that Mo exhibited obvious grain refinement effect in TiAl alloy. This effect probably originated from the low diffusion rate of Mo in TiAl matrix.
Therefore, it can be found that the addition of alloy element Mo leads to the lattice distortion of γ phase and α 2 phase, resulting in the effect of solid solution strengthening.
Classical Hall-Petch equation can be used to illustrate the grain refinement effect of Mo addition. The strengthening of grain boundary is due to dislocation pile-up at the grain boundaries.
Mo exhibits higher valence electron than O which could decrease oxygen vacancy concentration and decelerate the oxidation rate
Mo and Nb elements are free in the surface layer, and mainly distributed near the matrix which could hinder the diffusion of Ti and Al element to react with O
Mo is enriched near the TiAl matrix, reducing the oxygen solid solubility in the matrix, which may promote the formation of external Al 2 O 3 and inhibit internal oxidation.
